title: The determinant-one quadric of signature (2,2)
notes: For \(g=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\\gamma&\delta\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), the notes identify \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) with \(\alpha\delta-\beta\gamma=1\), then with \(x^2+y^2-z^2-t^2=1\).
statement: The linear substitution \(x=(\alpha+\delta)/2\), \(z=(\alpha-\delta)/2\), \(y=(\beta-\gamma)/2\), \(t=(\beta+\gamma)/2\) is invertible and satisfies \(\det g=x^2+y^2-z^2-t^2\). Thus \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) is precisely the nonsingular real level set of this quadratic form.
reconstruction: \ours\ The explicit change of coordinates is supplied here; expanding the four squares verifies the identification.
fate: This is the classical quadric model used again in \citet[pp.417--420]{gindikin2000integral}; it is background, not a 1976 novelty.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The identification is exact and elementary; no open question is attached to it.

title: Which linear symmetries come from left and right translations?
notes: The formula is \(g\mapsto g_1^{-1}gg_2\). The next sentence says that \emph{any} linear transformation preserving the hyperboloid has this form.
statement: For \(a,b\in SL(2,\mathbb R)\), \(X\mapsto aXb^{-1}\) gives a homomorphism onto \(SO_0(2,2)\), with kernel \(\{(I,I),(-I,-I)\}\). It does not exhaust \(O(2,2)\). For example \(X\mapsto X^{\mathsf T}\) preserves \(\det X\) but has determinant \(-1\) as a linear map on the four-dimensional matrix space.
reconstruction: \ours\ The transpose counterexample checks the literal quantifier. The notebook's inverse placement defines a right action on points; pullback \(T_{g_1,g_2}f(X)=f(g_1^{-1}Xg_2)\) is a representation on functions. These conventions should not be conflated.
fate: The left--right symmetry is standard in the real-quadric construction, as in \citet[pp.417--419]{gindikin2000integral}. The omitted identity-component restriction is a notebook error, not later progress.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected identity-component statement holds. The unrestricted statement remains false.

title: Stabilizers of points of the quadric
notes: The stabilizer of the identity is the diagonal subgroup, followed by the exercise ``compute the stabilizer subgroups of other points''.
statement: For \(x\in SL(2,\mathbb R)\), the pairs satisfying \(g_1^{-1}xg_2=x\) are exactly \(\{(xhx^{-1},h):h\in SL(2,\mathbb R)\}\). Hence every stabilizer is conjugate to the diagonal and \(G\simeq(G\times G)/\operatorname{diag}G\), with the action convention understood.
reconstruction: \ours\ Multiply the fixed-point equation by \(g_1\) on the left and by \(x^{-1}\) on the right. This solves the exercise completely.
fate: This is the elementary homogeneous-space structure underlying \citet[opening construction]{gindikin2000integral}; no independent research problem is created for the exercise.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Completely resolved by the displayed algebraic calculation.

title: Haar measure and the Hilbert space of the regular representation
notes: On \(\beta\ne0\), coordinates are \((\alpha,\delta,\beta)\), and \(dg=d\alpha\,d\beta\,d\delta/|\beta|\). The space is \(\mathcal H=L^2(G,dg)\).
statement: The measure \(\delta(\alpha\delta-\beta\gamma-1)\,d\alpha\,d\beta\,d\gamma\,d\delta\) is invariant under both determinant-one left and right multiplications. Integrating out \(\gamma=(\alpha\delta-1)/\beta\) gives the stated local Haar density, up to an overall positive constant. The left--right pullbacks are unitary on \(L^2(G)\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The delta-function calculation is the coarea identity on the chart \(\beta\ne0\); it does not claim that this single chart covers all of \(G\).
fate: The same invariant quadric measure is used in \citet[real geometry, pp.421--423]{gindikin2000integral}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard Haar measure; the chart restriction and normalization are essential but routine.

title: Separating series before decomposing into irreducibles
notes: The word ``irreducible'' is crossed out. Gelfand calls division into series algebraic and division of a series into representations transcendental; the example is explicitly said to be well known.
statement: For the left--right regular representation of \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\), seek invariant orthogonal projectors onto the closed sum \(L^2_{\rm disc}(G)\) of square-integrable discrete-series matrix-coefficient spaces and its continuous-spectrum orthogonal complement, and then onto the holomorphic and antiholomorphic discrete parts. The first question is coarser than specifying the Plancherel measure and every irreducible constituent.
reconstruction: The words ``algebraic'' and ``transcendental'' are a research preference, not a proved dichotomy. We formulate the definite projector problem using closed Hilbert subspaces.
fate: The spectral decomposition predates the talk: \citet[entry R18(a)]{strichartz1973hyperboloids} records the 1973 hyperboloid analysis. The specifically complex-analytic implementation is the subsequent \citet{gelfandgindikin1977complex}; its occurrences below receive class A.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The separation problem for this group is solved. Different analytic realizations must be distinguished from the older existence of the Plancherel decomposition.

title: Classification of real hyperplane sections
notes: For \(\xi\alpha+\eta\delta-p\beta-q\gamma=\zeta\), the notes classify sections using \(\Delta=\xi\eta-pq\). The degenerate case mixes ``hyperbolic paraboloid'', ``hyperbolic cylinder'' and a two-parameter label; P000661 gives paraboloids three parameters.
statement: Assume the normal covector is nonzero and identify proportional hyperplane equations. If \(\Delta<0\), the section is a one-sheeted hyperboloid. If \(\Delta>0\), it is one-sheeted, two-sheeted or a cone according as \(|\zeta|\) is greater than, less than or equal to \(2\sqrt\Delta\). If \(\Delta=0\), \(\zeta\ne0\) gives a hyperbolic paraboloid (three parameters), whereas \(\zeta=0\) gives a hyperbolic cylinder (two parameters). General nondegenerate sections have four parameters; tangent cones have three.
reconstruction: \ours\ For the null normal, reduce to \(\alpha=\zeta\). When \(\zeta\ne0\), \(\delta=(1+\beta\gamma)/\zeta\); when \(\zeta=0\), \(\beta\gamma=-1\) and \(\delta\) is free. This independently resolves the conflated degenerate cases.
fate: The section and horosphere geometry is treated in \citet[pp.418--423]{gindikin2000integral}; the underlying quadratic classification is elementary and predates the lecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Resolved with the null-level distinction. The two- and three-parameter families are different, not conflicting counts for one family.

title: The hyperplane Radon transform on the quadric
notes: The transform is \(\widehat\psi=\int_G\psi(g)\delta(\xi\alpha+\eta\delta-p\beta-q\gamma-\zeta)\,dg\), with \(\psi\in L^2(G)\) written without a domain qualification. The families \(A,B,D,E\) are then named.
statement: For \(\psi\in C_c^\infty(G)\), the displayed expression defines a distribution in the hyperplane parameters by pushforward; at transverse sections it is the usual surface integral with the coarea density. It is homogeneous of degree \(-1\) under simultaneous nonzero real scaling of the five parameters, with absolute value in the scaling factor. For general \(L^2\) input, pointwise surface integration requires a specified extension or regularization.
reconstruction: The test-function domain and distributional interpretation are supplied to avoid assigning a trace on a measure-zero surface to an arbitrary \(L^2\) equivalence class.
fate: Compare the precise transform domains in \citet[complex and real geometry]{gindikin2000integral}. The definition is classical; its unrestricted \(L^2\) pointwise reading is not.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Well defined on test functions and in appropriate distributional extensions. The notebook does not specify one extension on all of \(L^2(G)\).

title: The unspecified range of the four- and three-parameter transforms
notes: The question is \ru{Как описать, какие ф-и 4-х и 3-х перем. появляются?} No support, decay, regularity or boundary conditions are attached.
statement: A range problem would have to specify a source space \(X(G)\), one of the section families \(\mathcal F\), its density normalization, and a target space \(Y(\mathcal F)\), then characterize \(R_{\mathcal F}(X)\). These choices are missing, so there is no uniquely determined proposition here.
reconstruction: We do not replace this question by a familiar Euclidean range theorem, or identify inversion with surjectivity onto a characterized range.
fate: Targeted searches located \citet[main inversion construction]{gindikin2000integral}, but that does not identify the omitted function-space quantifiers. The 1977 Hardy theorem concerns a different, specified boundary-value problem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Unidentified at the exact range-theorem level. No assertion that it remains open, and no new problem-index entry, is justified.

title: Orthogonal discrete and continuous parts
notes: ``Main theorem 1'' begins \(\mathcal H=\mathcal H_A\overset\circ+\mathcal H_B\); the spaces were introduced as kernels of the two kinds of hyperplane integration.
statement: The unambiguous spectral statement is \(L^2(G)=L^2_{\rm disc}(G)\oplus L^2_{\rm cont}(G)\), an orthogonal decomposition invariant under both translations, where the first summand is the closed span of discrete-series matrix coefficients and the second its orthogonal complement. The identification of these summands with the notebook's integral kernels additionally requires precise domains for those transforms.
reconstruction: The spectral statement is separated from the more delicate kernel realization in the next occurrence. The circle over the plus sign is read as an orthogonal direct sum, consistently with the later projector discussion.
fate: The existence of the spectral decomposition precedes 1976; see the 1973 paper recorded in \citet[entry R18(a)]{strichartz1973hyperboloids}. The exact kernel formulations were not checked in that inaccessible article.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The spectral decomposition is established. Verification of this occurrence is indirect for the prior publication, not a claim to have read Strichartz's theorem.

title: Common kernels of the section and ruling transforms
notes: The notes assert \(\mathcal H_A=\mathcal H_D=\mathcal H_E=\mathcal H_C\), and label this the discrete series. Here \(C\) is the family of straight rulings.
statement: A standard precise part is the cuspidal characterization: take smooth Harish--Chandra Schwartz functions on \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) whose integrals \(\int_{\mathbb R}f(g_1^{-1}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)g_2)\,dt\) vanish for all \(g_1,g_2\). Their closure in \(L^2(G)\) is \(L^2_{\rm disc}(G)\). The additional equality with every hyperplane-kernel realization is a distinct announced claim; the notebook omits the realizations needed to state it on all \(L^2\).
reconstruction: The modern cuspidal interpretation supplies a well-defined part of the statement. We do not silently close the kernel on compactly supported functions, which need not recover the discrete spectrum.
fate: The historical identification is consistent with the pre-talk harmonic analysis and \citet[real horospherical transform]{gindikin2000integral}. An exact source proving all four kernel equalities with the notebook's unspecified conventions was not verified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The discrete/cuspidal identification is standard. The full notebook formulation receives only a partial publication match and medium confidence, not an invented unresolved-conjecture status.

title: An ultrahyperbolic equation for the transform
notes: The transformed function is said to satisfy a second-order ultrahyperbolic equation ``that can be written down'', but no operator is displayed.
statement: For the test-function transform above, in the sense of distributions, \[ (\partial_\xi\partial_\eta-\partial_p\partial_q-\partial_\zeta^2)\widehat\psi=0. \] Indeed differentiation under the integral inserts \(\alpha\delta-\beta\gamma-1=0\). Additional range conditions do not follow merely from this equation.
reconstruction: \ours\ The explicit PDE is reconstructed directly from the determinant equation; it is not a formula actually written in the notebook. The two minus signs in the \(p,q\) coefficients cancel in the mixed derivative.
fate: This is the classical differential constraint of a Radon transform supported on a quadric; compare the transform setting in \citet[pp.418--423]{gindikin2000integral}. The derivation here checks only the asserted necessary PDE.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The reconstructed necessary condition is proved directly. It is not a sufficient range characterization.

title: The unexplained minimality of the families A, D and E
notes: A separate sentence says \ru{Сем-ва A, D, E явл. минимальными}.
statement: No order on families, admissible restriction, local completeness notion or minimal parameter count is supplied. Consequently ``minimal'' cannot be converted into a uniquely testable theorem from this sentence alone.
reconstruction: Minimality under inclusion, minimal dimension for inversion, and minimality for detecting the continuous series are different assertions; none is selected editorially.
fate: The exact-phrase and horospherical searches led to \citet{gindikin2000integral}, but no precise claim matching this unqualified sentence was identified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Unidentified, rather than certified open or undeveloped.

title: Straight rulings as translates of a unipotent subgroup
notes: The examples are \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&z\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}h&z\\0&h^{-1}\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), and the general left--right translate; the ruling family has three parameters.
statement: Every affine real line contained in \(\det X=1\) is \(A(I+tN)\), where \(A\in SL(2,\mathbb R)\), \(N\ne0\), \(\operatorname{tr}N=\det N=0\). Thus \(N^2=0\), and up to reparametrization the line is a left--right translate of the upper unipotent subgroup. The space of unoriented lines has dimension three.
reconstruction: \ours\ Expand \(\det(A+tB)=1+t\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}B)+t^2\det(A^{-1}B)\). At each \(A\), null directions form a one-dimensional projective cone; subtracting the one line parameter from \(3+1\) gives dimension 3.
fate: These are the real horocycles in \citet[pp.418--422]{gindikin2000integral}; the classification follows by the elementary determinant calculation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The construction and count are exact, with zero direction excluded.

title: The two complex domains and the Siegel coordinate chart
notes: On the complex determinant-one quadric the inequality is \(\Im(\alpha\bar\beta)\Im(\delta\bar\beta)>(\Im\beta)^2\). The two signs are said to give domains with distinguished boundary \(G\); in three coordinates the boundary is called \(\mathbb R^3\).
statement: On \(\beta\ne0\), put \(Z=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\alpha/\beta&-1/\beta\\-1/\beta&\delta/\beta\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). The inequality is equivalent to \(\det\Im Z>0\), hence \(\Im Z\) is positive or negative definite. These are the two sign components in this chart. Their invariant continuation in \(SL(2,\mathbb C)\) has the real group as its distinguished boundary in the relevant Hardy realization. The chart omits \(Z_{12}=0\); neither this parametrization nor the phrase \(\mathbb R^3\) identifies the entire group with one Euclidean chart.
reconstruction: \ours\ The coordinate calculation multiplies \(\det\Im Z\) by \(|\beta|^4\). ``Distinguished boundary'' requires a specified holomorphic function algebra or Hardy norm; it is not defined for arbitrary unbounded holomorphic functions solely by uniqueness.
fate: \citet[\S 3, Proposition~5]{gelfandgindikin1977complex} publishes the same inequality and domain construction in 1977, after the 1976 talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The invariant domain realization is established; the global chart and function-class qualifications must accompany the notebook shorthand.

title: A distinguished boundary is more than a uniqueness set
notes: The parenthetical definition calls the skeleton the smallest boundary set from which a holomorphic function continuous on the closure is uniquely recovered.
statement: For a unital uniform algebra \(\mathcal A\subset C(K)\) on a compact Hausdorff space, the Shilov boundary is the smallest closed set \(S\subset K\) such that \(\|f\|_K=\sup_S|f|\) for every \(f\in\mathcal A\). Mere uniqueness is weaker: for the disc algebra, every nontrivial closed boundary arc is a uniqueness set, whereas the Shilov boundary is the whole circle. Two disjoint such arcs show that a smallest uniqueness set need not exist.
reconstruction: \ours\ Boundary vanishing on an arc gives analytic continuation by Schwarz reflection and then the identity theorem. Conversely, \((1+\bar\zeta z)/2\) peaks at any prescribed unit-circle point \(\zeta\), forcing every closed norming boundary to contain the whole circle. For the unbounded seminar domains one must specify the function class or compactification.
fate: The classical minimal closed norming-boundary definition is recalled precisely in \citet[\S 1]{acosta2006boundaries}. The notebook's uniqueness-only definition is not equivalent to it.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The standard definition is established; the literal uniqueness-only definition is false in this generality.
area: Several complex variables and function algebras

title: Hardy boundary values separate the two discrete series
notes: ``Main theorem 2'' says \(\psi\in\mathcal H_A\) iff \(\psi=\psi_++\psi_-\), where the two functions continue analytically to \(D_+,D_-\). It also asserts zero intersection because everything is in \(L^2\).
statement: Let \(H^2(D_\pm)\) be the invariant Hardy spaces with uniformly bounded \(L^2(G)\) norms on interior translates approaching the real distinguished boundary. Their boundary maps are isometries onto the holomorphic and antiholomorphic discrete-series summands \(H_\pm\). These summands are orthogonal, \(H_+\cap H_-=0\), and \(L^2_{\rm disc}(G)=H_+\oplus H_-\). Mere holomorphic continuation, without the Hardy bound and the specified boundary-value sense, is insufficient as a definition.
reconstruction: The Hardy condition and boundary-limit interpretation are restored from the published theorem; they are not written in the notebook.
fate: The precise statement appears in \citet[Theorem~3, Proposition~4 and \S 4]{gelfandgindikin1977complex}, received 6 June 1977.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for the specified Hardy spaces. The later continuous-series cohomological realization should not be substituted for this discrete-series theorem.

title: The holomorphic projector kernel and its missing trace factor
notes: The written kernel is \(c[2-\alpha_1\delta_2-\delta_1\alpha_2+\gamma_1\beta_2+\beta_1\gamma_2]^{-3/2}=c[2-\operatorname{tr}(g_1g_2^{-1})]^{-3/2}\). Both scan and transcriptions have just this factor.
statement: For the invariant Haar normalization used in the published discrete-series projector, write \(t=\operatorname{tr}(g_1g_2^{-1})=\lambda+\lambda^{-1}\), choosing the holomorphic eigenvalue branch \(|\lambda|>1\) in the relevant semigroup. Up to a nonzero normalization constant and its consistent branch, the kernel is \[K=c\frac{\lambda^2}{(\lambda-1)^3(\lambda+1)}=c[(t-2)^3(t+2)]^{-1/2}.\] Its distributional boundary value gives the orthogonal projector. The extra factor \((t+2)^{-1/2}\) cannot be absorbed in \(c\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ Summing the character series gives \[\frac{\sum_{n\ge1}n\lambda^{-n}}{\lambda-\lambda^{-1}}=\frac{\lambda^2}{(\lambda-1)^3(\lambda+1)}.\] Squaring and substituting \(t=\lambda+\lambda^{-1}\) verifies the trace expression independently. The full derivation and rational/numerical checks are preserved in the critical audit.
fate: \citet[\S 4, Theorem~10, equations~18 and 22]{gelfandgindikin1977complex} gives the corrected kernel in 1977. This is a precise publication match to the construction, with a literal notebook error.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The corrected projector is established. The notebook's displayed formula is not the same invariant kernel even after constant renormalization.

title: The Fourier-integral technique behind the projector
notes: The concluding heading calls the ``submerged part'' Fourier-integral technique and describes \(K\) as an analogue of the Cauchy kernel.
statement: In the verified construction, discrete-series characters are analytically continued into the semigroup and summed with their Plancherel weights to obtain a holomorphic reproducing kernel; its boundary value acts as a projection on \(L^2(G)\). This is a concrete implementation of the Cauchy-kernel analogy, not a separate general theorem about Fourier integral operators.
reconstruction: The character-series procedure is supplied by the publication. The notebook itself records only the method label, with no phase, amplitude or symbol calculus.
fate: \citet[\S 4, equations~15--22]{gelfandgindikin1977complex} supplies the precise construction in 1977.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The bounded method claim is identified. No broader Fourier-integral-operator theorem is attributed to this one sentence.

title: Arnold’s Möbius characterization of the two domains
notes: Arnold conjectures that \(D_+\) consists of transformations taking the disc into itself and \(D_-\) of transformations taking its exterior into itself. The last line says \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) preserves the circle.
statement: After Cayley conjugation from the real-projective-line/upper-half-plane model to the unit-circle model, the relevant open domains are the strict Möbius contraction semigroups: one sends the closed unit disc into the open disc, and the other sends the closed exterior in \(\mathbb{CP}^1\) into the open exterior. Their real edge is the circle-preserving form conjugate to \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\), modulo its central kernel. Without conjugation, the standard real matrices preserve \(\mathbb{RP}^1\), not the standard unit circle.
reconstruction: The words ``strict'', the compactified exterior and the Cayley change of real form are required to distinguish the open domains from the semigroup boundary.
fate: \citet[\S 3, Proposition~9]{gelfandgindikin1977complex} proves precisely this geometric identification in 1977.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Resolved by the 1977 proposition, with the model and strictness qualifications above.
speaker: V. I. Arnold

title: The graded Weil algebra
notes: \(W(\mathfrak g)=\Lambda^*(\mathfrak g')\otimes S^*(\mathfrak g')\), viewed as functions of \(2n\) variables, with \(\Lambda^p\otimes S^q\) in degree \(p+2q\).
statement: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g\) over \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\), \(W(\mathfrak g)\) is the free graded-commutative algebra on odd generators \(\theta^i\) of cohomological degree 1 and even generators \(u^i\) of degree 2, two copies of \(\mathfrak g^*\). Thus its underlying superdimension is \(n|n\); ``functions'' here means polynomials in the even variables and exterior polynomials in the odd ones.
reconstruction: The field, finite-dimensionality and polynomial interpretation are supplied. No smooth or completed function algebra is implied.
fate: The construction is already in \citet[Expos\'e~19, Weil-algebra construction]{cartan1950weil}, delivered 15 May 1950.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard definition. The earlier discussion of superfunctions in 1975-389.1 supplies context but is not the same construction.

title: The Chevalley differential sign convention
notes: For \(h\in\Lambda^\ell\mathfrak g^*\), the displayed sum is \[\sum_{i<j}(-1)^{i+j-1}h([g_i,g_j],g_1,\ldots,\widehat g_i,\ldots,\widehat g_j,\ldots).\] In degree 1 it is \(h([g_1,g_2])\).
statement: With one-based argument indices, define \(d_+h\) by exactly that alternating sum. It is the negative of the frequently used trivial-coefficient Chevalley--Eilenberg differential, so \(d_+^2=0\) by Jacobi and it obeys the graded Leibniz rule. Either overall sign convention computes the same cohomology.
reconstruction: The remaining arguments retain their original order after the two omissions. The positive bracket sign is internally consistent and is not a transcription error.
fate: Compare the exterior differential within the pre-existing Weil construction of \citet[Expos\'e~19]{cartan1950weil}; the overall sign is conventional.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct with the stated indexing and sign convention.

title: The unique Weil differential on both sets of generators
notes: The differential sends \(h\otimes1\) to \((d_+h)\otimes1+1\otimes h\), is a graded derivation, and is said to extend uniquely with square zero. P000664 gives \(d(1\otimes h^k)=c_{ij}^{k}(h^i\otimes h^j)\).
statement: If \([e_i,e_j]=c_{ij}^{k}e_k\), the notebook's sign convention gives \[d\theta^k=\tfrac12c_{ij}^{k}\theta^i\theta^j+u^k,\qquad du^k=c_{ij}^{k}\theta^iu^j.\] Together with \(d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{\deg a}a\,d(b)\), these formulas define a unique degree-one derivation satisfying \(d^2=0\). The second formula is forced by \(d^2\theta^k=0\); Jacobi then gives \(d^2u^k=0\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The factor \(1/2\) arises from summing over all ordered pairs \(i,j\); it disappears if one sums only \(i<j\). We have checked the sign of \(du\) against the notebook's positive exterior differential.
fate: This is the Weil differential of \citet[Expos\'e~19]{cartan1950weil}, with an explicitly reconciled sign convention, not a new 1976 construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct. The two tensor factors in the structure-constant formula have degrees 1 and 2, respectively.

title: Acyclicity in positive degree, with constants surviving
notes: The ``main theorem'' says that the homologies of the complex are zero, without a qualification on degree.
statement: For the unaugmented cochain algebra above, \(H^0(W(\mathfrak g),d)=\mathbb K\) and \(H^j(W(\mathfrak g),d)=0\) for \(j>0\). Equivalently, the augmentation \(W(\mathfrak g)\to\mathbb K\) is a quasi-isomorphism.
reconstruction: \ours\ Put \(v^i=d\theta^i\). This is an invertible triangular replacement of the even generators; now \(d\theta^i=v^i\), \(dv^i=0\). The odd operator \(h=\sum_i\theta^i\partial/\partial v^i\) satisfies \(dh+hd=N\), where \(N\) counts the total number of generators. Division by positive \(N\) contracts every positive-weight component, but not the constant 1.
fate: \citet[Expos\'e~20, \S 2, Theorem~1]{cartan1950transgression} states the precise acyclicity result in 1950.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The positive-degree theorem is established; literal vanishing in degree 0 is false. The notebook also says ``homologies'' although its differential raises degree.

title: Computing compact Lie-group cohomology from invariant forms
notes: Kirillov says that the algebra was devised for computing the homologies of simple compact Lie groups, and that invariant symmetric forms are easier to find than skew-symmetric ones.
statement: For a compact connected Lie group \(K\) over \(\mathbb R\), averaging identifies de Rham cohomology with the cohomology of invariant forms; bi-invariant forms give the harmonic representatives for a bi-invariant metric. The cohomology algebra is exterior on primitive odd-degree generators. Invariant polynomials \((S\mathfrak k^*)^K\), together with transgression, determine their degrees. Simplicity is not needed for this real-coefficient statement.
reconstruction: Connectedness, compactness and real coefficients are explicit. This does not assert an integral-cohomology computation, where torsion is invisible to differential forms.
fate: \citet[Expos\'e~20, \S\S 3--4]{cartan1950transgression} supplies the transgression method before 1976.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established real-coefficient theory. The method statement is distinct from the incorrect unrestricted counting rule in the next occurrence.

title: Primitive odd forms versus indecomposable symmetric invariants
notes: The conclusion reads: as many invariant skew-symmetric forms of degree \(k\) as symmetric ones of degree \((k+1)/2\). A preceding sentence calls an odd form the differential of a symmetric expression.
statement: Let \(I=(S\mathfrak k^*)^K\), \(I^+\) its positive-degree ideal, and \(Q(I)=I^+/(I^+)^2\). For compact connected \(K\), transgression identifies \(Q(I)_m\) with the primitive part of \(H^{2m-1}(K;\mathbb R)\), up to the usual choice of generators. A degree-\(m\) invariant polynomial has Weil degree \(2m\) and is \(d\) of a transgression element of degree \(2m-1\), whose exterior component represents the corresponding primitive class. The differential direction in the notebook must therefore be reversed.
reconstruction: \ours\ For \(K=SU(2)\), the square of the Killing quadratic polynomial is a nonzero invariant symmetric polynomial of degree 4, whereas \(\Lambda^7\mathfrak{su}(2)^*=0\). This disproves the literal count at \(k=7\), while its indecomposable version is correct.
fate: The corrected generator correspondence is \citet[Expos\'e~20, \S 4, Theorem~2]{cartan1950transgression}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established for primitive and indecomposable generators. The unrestricted equality and the displayed differential direction are false as written.

title: When can a scalar second-order ODE be straightened by point transformations?
notes: For \(y''=F(x,y,y')\), Arnold asks whether solution curves can be straightened. The page explicitly cites Tresse 1896 and Acta Mathematica 1894, and contrasts general equations with \(y''=0\).
statement: For a smooth scalar equation on an open set in \((x,y,p)\), local equivalence under a nonsingular point change \((x,y)\mapsto(X,Y)\), on a chart where \(dX/dx\ne0\), to \(Y_{XX}=0\) holds exactly when the two relative invariants vanish identically there: \[I=F_{pppp},\quad H=D^2F_{pp}-4DF_{yp}-F_pDF_{pp}+6F_{yy}-3F_yF_{pp}+4F_pF_{yp},\qquad D=\partial_x+p\partial_y+F\partial_p.\] Vanishing at one point is insufficient; these are local identities on an open set.
reconstruction: The displayed criterion and smooth regular setting are modern precision supplied from the classical equivalence theory, not formulas written on P000664.
fate: \citet[\S 2, \S 4.1]{kruglikov2009tresse} reconstructs the Lie--Liouville--Tresse criterion and its nineteenth-century provenance. Cartan's 1924 treatment reaches the same flatness test geometrically \citep[\S VIII, no.24]{cartan1924projective}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The local point-linearization problem is solved. The 2008 preprint/2009 exposition is not the first circulation of the classical result.

title: Every linear second-order equation is locally point-flat
notes: The notes state that \(y''+a(x)y'+b(x)y=0\) becomes \(y''=0\) after a change of independent variable and a change linear in \(y\); configuration theorems such as Desargues are then transferred to the solution family.
statement: Let \(a,b\) be smooth on an interval and let \(u,v\) be independent solutions, with \(v\ne0\) on a smaller interval. Then \(X=u/v\), \(Y=y/v\) is a local point diffeomorphism because \(X'=W/v^2\ne0\), and every solution becomes \(Y=c_1X+c_2\). Any incidence theorem formulated for straight-line configurations transfers to configurations lying wholly in this coordinate neighbourhood; no global straightening across zeros or monodromy is asserted.
reconstruction: \ours\ The ratio-of-solutions proof also states the actual domain restriction. The doubtful Russian phrase translated ``linear menu'' is not used to infer extra content.
fate: This classical fact is recalled in \citet[introduction]{kruglikov2009tresse}; Arnold presents it explicitly as old material.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Completely established locally. The incidence-theorem remark is a consequence of transporting points and curves by this diffeomorphism.

title: Cartan geometry of a general second-order equation
notes: Cartan 1924--25 is invoked: solutions are geodesics of a projective connection. The next lines pass to the space of line elements \((x,y,y')\).
statement: A regular second-order equation defines a path geometry on the three-dimensional contact-element space and has a canonical normal Cartan connection of projective path-geometry type. It descends to an ordinary projective equivalence class of torsion-free affine connections on the two-dimensional point space precisely when \(F\) is cubic or lower in \(p=y'\). Thus a projective connection on contact elements and one on points are different notions.
reconstruction: We preserve the passage to contact elements rather than automatically declaring the general-\(F\) sentence false. The surface-connection reading requires the cubic condition recorded later on P000666.
fate: \citet[introduction and \S\S VII--VIII, especially nos.22--24]{cartan1924projective} explicitly distinguishes the two geometries and proves the general contact-element construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established; the distinction prevents importing an affine-geodesic claim for arbitrary \(F\).

title: Two transverse line fields spanning a contact distribution
notes: Arnold says that reducing a pair of direction fields in \(\mathbb R^3\) under diffeomorphisms is equivalent to the ODE problem, then remarks that their span is a contact structure.
statement: Let \(L,V\) be an ordered pair of smooth rank-one distributions on a three-manifold, transverse at the point, with \(L\oplus V\) contact. Locally choose contact coordinates \((x,y,p)\) in which \(V=\langle\partial_p\rangle\) and \(L=\langle\partial_x+p\partial_y+F\partial_p\rangle\). Local diffeomorphisms preserving the ordered pair correspond to point transformations on the local leaf space of \(V\), with their prolongations. Arbitrary pairs whose span is integrable are excluded.
reconstruction: The rank, ordering, contact and local leaf-space assumptions are restored explicitly. Exchanging the two fields gives the dual equation rather than the same point-equivalence problem.
fate: The contact-element formulation and duality are in \citet[\S VII and \S VIII, no.23]{cartan1924projective}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The regular contact version is exact. Without the contact hypothesis the announced equivalence is false.

title: A projective parameter along each solution
notes: After choosing one solution as \(y=0\), the linear part is straightened by \(\widetilde x=f(x)\), \(\widetilde y=g(x)y\). The function \(f\) satisfies a Schwarz-type equation, and a projective structure is said to arise on every solution.
statement: Along a smooth solution \(y_0\), infinitesimal transverse variations satisfy \(\eta''=F_p(x,y_0,y_0')\eta'+F_y(x,y_0,y_0')\eta\). If \(u,v\) are independent Jacobi solutions, \([u(x):v(x)]\in\mathbb{RP}^1\) gives a local projective coordinate; changing the Jacobi basis changes it by a Möbius map. For \(\eta''+a\eta'+b\eta=0\), its affine ratio satisfies \(S(f)=2b-a'-a^2/2\), where \(S(f)=f^{(3)}/f'-\tfrac32(f''/f')^2\).
reconstruction: \ours\ Removing the first derivative by \(\eta=e^{-\frac12\int a}z\) gives \(z''+(b-a'/2-a^2/4)z=0\); the ratio identity proves the Schwarzian formula. The construction is local along a nonsingular solution.
fate: This is the projective parametrization inherent in the classical connection theory \citep[\S\S VII--VIII]{cartan1924projective}; the notebook explains it through linearization rather than a new existence theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established locally. Global holonomy and the topology of closed solutions are additional data, not determined by this local construction.

title: Inequivalent projective structures on the circle
notes: The standard \(\mathbb{RP}^1\) and its pullback under a degree-two covering \(S^1\to\mathbb{RP}^1\) are called inequivalent. Arnold proposes examining infinitesimal automorphisms \(\partial_x,x\partial_x,x^2\partial_x\).
statement: For each positive integer \(n\), pull back the projective atlas on \(\mathbb{RP}^1\) by the degree-\(n\) covering. The resulting circle structures are pairwise inequivalent under projective-structure-preserving diffeomorphisms. In an angular coordinate their infinitesimal projective automorphism fields are spanned by \(\partial_\theta,\sin(n\theta)\partial_\theta,\cos(n\theta)\partial_\theta\). A nonzero such field can have at most \(2n\) distinct zeros, and the maximum is achieved.
reconstruction: \ours\ The zero-count maximum is preserved by diffeomorphisms, distinguishing \(n=1\) from \(n=2\) as the notebook requests. The abstract Lie algebra is \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) in both cases; its realization on the circle, not its abstract isomorphism type, distinguishes them.
fate: This is an elementary consequence of the classical projective action; \citet[projective frame construction]{cartan1924projective} supplies the historical framework. No complete classification of all circle projective structures is claimed here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The two stated examples, and their covering generalization, are rigorously distinguished by the displayed argument.

title: The damaged global projective-structure question
notes: The line marked ``Problem'' contains two cancellations and survives only as a question involving ``the equation'', ``globally'' and ``locally projective space''. The scan does not recover the missing relation.
statement: No unique global problem is recoverable. It might concern developing maps, holonomy, realization of a projective circle as a solution, or global equivalence of path geometries; these have different objects and answers.
reconstruction: The list of possible readings explains the uncertainty and is not a proposed reconstruction of Arnold's question.
fate: Searches of the exact local-projective vocabulary and Cartan/Arnold sources did not resolve the deleted words. \citet{cartan1924projective} supplies context only.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Unidentified from the source; no open-problem or nondevelopment claim is made.

title: Removing the mixed quadratic transverse terms
notes: After linear straightening, \(y''=a(x)y^2+b(x)yy'+c(x)y'^2+\cdots\). Coordinate changes \(\widetilde x=x+yf(x,y)\), \(\widetilde y=y(1+yg(x,y))\) are said to kill \(b,c\).
statement: Work locally near \(y=p=0\) with zero constant and linear transverse terms. Up to terms of total degree at least 3 in \((y,p)\), use \(X=x+f(x)y\), \(Y=y+g(x)y^2\). The new quadratic coefficients are \(a+g''\), \(b+4g'-f''\), \(c+2g-2f'\). Choosing \(g=f'-c/2\) and \(f''=(2c'-b)/3\) removes the last two and leaves \[A=a+\tfrac16c''-\tfrac13b'.\] The coordinate Jacobian equals 1 along the reference solution.
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ The explicit coefficient formulas, local integrations for \(f,g\), and the stated jet order are editorial calculations. No convergence of an infinite normal-form process is inferred.
fate: The residual coefficient is \(H/12\) on the normalized solution, where \(H\) is the classical Tresse invariant reviewed in \citet[\S 2.1]{kruglikov2009tresse}. This identifies the old invariant behind the notebook calculation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The finite-order elimination is verified algebraically. The normalization does not itself settle all higher-order terms.

title: The relative 5/2-density along a solution
notes: The remaining coefficient is written \(a(x)(dx)^{5/2}\), defined up to a multiplicative constant depending on the solution.
statement: Let \(A\) be the residual quadratic coefficient after the preceding normalization. On an oriented projective coordinate interval, the residual transformations preserving the flat variational equation have \(X=\phi(x)\), \(Y=k\sqrt{\phi'(x)}\,y+O(y^2)\), with \(\phi\) Möbius, \(\phi'>0\), \(k\ne0\). After renormalizing mixed quadratic terms, \(\widetilde A=A/(k(\phi')^{5/2})\), so \(A(dx)^{5/2}\) is determined up to the constant factor \(k^{-1}\). For unoriented real coordinates use the corresponding density bundle.
reconstruction: \ours\ The weight is checked by the transformation of the normalized equation. The notation denotes a tensor density, not an ordinary differential form of noninteger exterior degree; its scale is not canonically fixed.
fate: It is the solutionwise form of the classical relative invariant \(H\) in \citet[\S 2.1, weights]{kruglikov2009tresse}. An exact later Arnold publication of this particular normalization was not verified; the invariant identification, rather than that unverified lead, supports class E.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The local relative-density statement is well defined with orientation and scale specified.

title: Why vanishing on one solution does not imply formal straightening
notes: The recorded theorem says that if \(a(x)(dx)^{5/2}\equiv0\), the equation can be straightened in formal series. The page has just fixed a single solution; no ``all solutions'' or cubic hypothesis is stated in the theorem line.
statement: Taken along one chosen solution, the implication is false: \(y''=y^3\) has the solution \(y=0\), zero linear and quadratic transverse parts, and hence zero displayed density there, but its Tresse invariant is \(H=36y\), a nonzero formal series. It is therefore not formally point-equivalent to \(Y''=0\) near that solution. A sufficient corrected condition is the simultaneous formal vanishing of \(I,H\); in the cubic-in-\(p\) class, vanishing of \(H\) on an open set suffices because \(I=0\).
reconstruction: \ours\ This counterexample audits the strongest literal interpretation supported by the neighbouring sentences. We do not claim it disproves an unstated theorem about a family of all solutions with additional assumptions.
fate: The obstruction is already part of classical point equivalence \citep[\S 2 and \S 4.1]{kruglikov2009tresse}; the notebook's abbreviated implication is not a new unresolved conjecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: False under the one-solution reading. The source does not determine which extra quantifiers Arnold intended.

title: The normal form with a squared first derivative factor
notes: Further diffeomorphisms are said to lead to \(y''=y'^2A(x,y,y')\).
statement: Every regular smooth scalar second-order equation admits this form locally near a chosen initial direction after a point transformation. First choose a local foliation by solutions and use its leaf label as \(y\), obtaining \(F(x,y,0)=0\). Then put \(X=\phi(x,y)\), \(Y=y\), with \(\phi_x\ne0\) and \(\phi_{xx}=F_p(x,y,0)\phi_x\). The transformed right side has both value and first \(P\)-derivative zero at \(P=0\), hence equals \(P^2A(X,Y,P)\) by smooth division.
reconstruction: \ours\ The foliation exists by the local ODE existence theorem and a transverse initial curve. The second coordinate change is obtained by integrating a linear equation for \(\phi_x\), choosing it nonzero. This proof supplies the precise local scope omitted in the notes.
fate: This is a local coordinate normalization within the classical path-geometry equivalence problem \citep[\S\S VII--VIII]{cartan1924projective}, not a criterion for flatness.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The local finite normalization is verified. It does not make the arbitrary coefficient \(A\) vanish and imposes no global reduction.

title: Cubic slope equations form an invariant projective class
notes: The equation \(y''=P_3(y')\), with coefficients depending on \(x,y\), is said to be invariant under plane diffeomorphisms and is associated with R. Liouville.
statement: The class \(F=A_0(x,y)+A_1(x,y)p+A_2(x,y)p^2+A_3(x,y)p^3\) is preserved by local point transformations wherever the transformed independent variable is valid. Exactly these equations describe the unparametrized geodesics of torsion-free affine connections on a surface, modulo projective equivalence \(\widehat\nabla_XY=\nabla_XY+\alpha(X)Y+\alpha(Y)X\).
reconstruction: The coefficients may vary on the surface; ``third degree'' means degree at most 3. The graph-coordinate restriction excludes directions sent to vertical ones.
fate: \citet[introduction, \S VIII no.24]{cartan1924projective} explicitly gives the cubic criterion; \citet[\S 4.1]{kruglikov2009tresse} supplies a modern account of Lie and Liouville's earlier work.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established projective differential geometry, already classical in 1976.

title: A vector field from a nonvanishing relative density
notes: The scalar-invariant discussion begins with \(v(x)=a(x)^{-2/5}\partial_x\).
statement: On an oriented interval where the real density coefficient \(A\) is nowhere zero, choose a consistent fifth-root convention and set \(v=A^{-2/5}\partial_x\). Under coordinate changes this is a vector field. Rescaling the original density by a nonzero constant rescales \(v\) by a constant; at zeros of \(A\) the formula is singular and provides no smooth invariant field.
reconstruction: The nonvanishing and branch qualifications, and the residual constant ambiguity, are necessary. They prevent treating this as a globally defined absolute invariant of every equation.
fate: This is algebra on the classical relative invariant identified in \citet[\S 2.1]{kruglikov2009tresse}, not an independent classification theorem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Well defined only on the stated nonvanishing locus, up to the inherited constant.

title: The projective scalar I2 and the adjoint quadratic form
notes: The notebook says that the projective group acts on two-jets by the adjoint representation and writes \(I_2=2v''v-v'^2\).
statement: For a specified smooth vector field \(v(x)\partial_x\) on a projective line, \(I_2(v)=2vv''-(v')^2\) is a scalar invariant under Möbius changes. More generally, if \(X=\phi(x)\), \(V(X)=\phi'(x)v(x)\), then \[2VV_{XX}-V_X^2=2vv''-v'^2+2v^2S(\phi).\] The quadratic polynomial vector fields form \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) under the usual bracket; evaluating their two-jet at a point gives an isomorphism, and \(I_2\) is the corresponding discriminant/Killing quadratic form up to normalization.
reconstruction: \ours\ The transformation identity proves invariance since \(S(\phi)=0\) for Möbius maps. A pointed two-jet includes a base point; the notebook's adjoint statement refers to the induced identification of its three coefficient coordinates with a quadratic projective vector field.
fate: This is classical projective invariant theory; the Cartan framework predates the talk \citep{cartan1924projective}. The displayed identity is independently checked in the audit rather than attributed to an unread formula in a later text.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Correct for a specified vector field and projective coordinate changes. Its value scales by \(c^2\) under \(v\mapsto cv\), so it is not absolute for the unnormalized ODE density.

title: Invariant differentiation and the higher In
notes: The recurrence is \(I_3=vI_2'\), then \(I_n=vI_{n-1}'\).
statement: The operator \(\nabla_v=v(x)d/dx\) is coordinate invariant. Starting from the Möbius scalar \(I_2\), define \(I_n=\nabla_v^{n-2}I_2\) for \(n\ge3\); each is a scalar invariant of the specified vector field on the projective line. If \(v\) is rescaled by a constant \(c\), then \(I_n\) is rescaled by \(c^n\). No completeness or functional independence of this list is claimed.
reconstruction: \ours\ Coordinate invariance follows from \(V\partial_X=v\partial_x\). Induction proves the scaling law, recording exactly the ambiguity inherited from the density.
fate: Invariant differentiation is part of the classical differential-invariant calculus reviewed in \citet[\S 1--2]{kruglikov2009tresse}. The notebook's narrower recurrence is verified directly here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The recurrence is correct with its scale qualification; it is not a complete classification of second-order equations.

title: Gelfand’s proposed connection with Gelfand–Fuchs cohomology
notes: The final line says \ru{Гипотеза Гельфанда: связано с когомологиями Гельфанда--Фукса}. Pommaret is then mentioned as having worked on differential invariants.
statement: The source specifies neither a Lie algebra/module, a cohomological degree, a cocycle nor a map relating cohomology to the displayed invariants. Consequently no definite conjecture with verifiable quantifiers can be extracted.
reconstruction: The cohomological terminology is retained as a proposed connection. It is not automatically identified with the Virasoro cocycle, the Schwarzian cocycle or an arbitrary theorem about formal vector fields.
fate: Targeted searches of the 5/2-density, projective-vector-field invariants and Gelfand--Fuchs terminology did not identify an exact statement. \citet{kruglikov2009tresse} matches the differential-invariant side only.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Unidentified as a precise conjecture. No C/D classification or development claim is warranted.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Lie superalgebra signs and parity
notes: \(L=L_0\oplus L_1\), \([a,b]=(-1)^{da\,db+1}[b,a]\), and Jacobi ``with signs''. The first definition writes \(da=\dim a\), while the continuation correctly writes \(\operatorname{deg}a\).
statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, a Lie superalgebra is a \(\mathbb Z/2\)-graded vector space with a bilinear degree-zero bracket, satisfying for homogeneous elements \([a,b]=-(-1)^{|a||b|}[b,a]\) and \((-1)^{|a||c|}[a,[b,c]]+(-1)^{|b||a|}[b,[c,a]]+(-1)^{|c||b|}[c,[a,b]]=0\). The number \(|a|\) is parity, not vector-space dimension.
reconstruction: The complete Jacobi formula and homogeneous-element qualification are supplied. The subsequent manuscript line decides the intended meaning of \(da\).
fate: \citet[\S 2]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields} gives the pre-talk algebraic framework. The seminar had already treated Lie superalgebras in 1975-389.5.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Standard definition; the dimensional notation is a faithful local error resolved by the next page.

title: The associative supercommutator
notes: Even-even and even-odd brackets are commutators; odd-odd brackets are anticommutators in an associative matrix algebra.
statement: For an associative \(\mathbb Z/2\)-graded algebra \(A\) with \(A_iA_j\subset A_{i+j}\), \([a,b]_s=ab-(-1)^{|a||b|}ba\) defines a Lie superalgebra. Any graded linear subspace closed under this bracket is a Lie subsuperalgebra. A matrix example requires a chosen grading, such as the block grading of \(\operatorname{End}(V_0\oplus V_1)\). Closure under associative multiplication is not required for the subsuperalgebra.
reconstruction: The grading of the ambient associative algebra is made explicit; arbitrary ungraded matrix subspaces with an assigned parity need not work.
fate: This standard realization is used in \citet[\S 2]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}; see also the earlier occurrence 1975-389.5.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established directly by expanding the graded Jacobi identity.

title: Real Majorana spinors in signature (-,+,+,+)
notes:
The metric is \(\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)\), the spinor space is explicitly corrected to real dimension 4, and four real matrices satisfy \(\gamma_\mu\gamma_
u+\gamma_
u\gamma_\mu=2\eta_{\mu
u}\). A barred spinor is written by multiplication by \(\gamma_0\).
statement: For this signature, the real Clifford algebra \(\mathrm{Cl}(3,1)\) is isomorphic to \(M_4(\mathbb R)\) and acts on a four-dimensional real Majorana module \(S\). One may choose \(\gamma_0\) antisymmetric and \(\gamma_i\) symmetric. A charge-conjugation bilinear pairing must be specified when converting a column spinor to a row; for a compatible real basis one can write \(\bar s=s^{\mathsf T}C\). The covariance formulas depend on this convention.
reconstruction: The transpose and charge-conjugation matrix distinguish the algebraic pairing from an unexplained row/column product. ``Approximately quaternions'' is only an analogy, not the Clifford-algebra identification.
fate: The Majorana conventions used for the component theory are discussed in \citet[\S 3 and Appendix]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The real four-component construction is correct for the stated signature; barred-index formulas require a pairing convention.

title: The four-dimensional supertranslation algebra
notes: After crossing out ``Poincar\'e'', the even part is translations; the odd part is spinors, with \([L_0,L_1]=0\) and \([\bar Q_i,\bar Q_j]=-2(\gamma^\mu)_{ij}P_\mu\).
statement: Let \(V=\mathbb R^{1,3}\) and \(S\) a real Majorana spin module. A nonzero \(\operatorname{Spin}(1,3)\)-equivariant symmetric map \(\beta:S\otimes S\to V\) defines a Lie superalgebra \(V\oplus S\) by \([s,t]=\beta(s,t)\), with \(V\) central. In a Majorana matrix formula the symmetric matrices are \(C\gamma^\mu\), with indices placed consistently. Equivalently, the complex Weyl notation has \(\{Q_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta}\}=2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\), \(\{Q,Q\}=\{\bar Q,\bar Q\}=0\).
reconstruction: The invariant pairing and normalizations replace the notebook's unqualified two-lowered-index gamma matrix. Because odd brackets land in the central even space, the three-odd Jacobi identity is immediate.
fate: The pre-talk construction appears in \citet[\S 2]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}; the 1971 algebra is reproduced in \citet[Appendix, equation~1]{likhtman2001supersymmetry}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established supertranslation algebra. It has four even translations and four real odd generators, before Lorentz generators are added.

title: Extending supertranslations to the Poincaré superalgebra
notes: Gelfand asks to extend the Poincar\'e algebra to a superalgebra. The preceding historical sentence names ``Gelfand and Likhtman''.
statement: Adjoin \(\mathfrak{so}(1,3)\) to the supertranslation algebra by its vector action on \(V\) and spin action \(\rho\) on \(S\): \(\mathfrak s=\mathfrak{so}(1,3)\ltimes(V\oplus S)\), \([M,s]=\rho(M)s\). The \(\mathfrak{so}(1,3)\)-equivariance of \(\beta\) is exactly the mixed Jacobi condition. Thus \(\mathfrak s_0=\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)\), \(\mathfrak s_1=S\), giving the four-dimensional \(N=1\) super-Poincar\'e algebra without central charges.
reconstruction: The request is interpreted as the existence/construction problem actually written, not a classification of all possible extensions. The historical name is Yu. A. Gol'fand, not the seminar's I. M. Gelfand.
fate: \citet[Appendix, equation~1 and release note]{likhtman2001supersymmetry} reproduces a preprint passed for printing 12 April 1971; its references identify the Gol'fand--Likhtman 1971 publication. The requested extension was therefore already known before this talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Solved by the displayed semidirect construction; not a 1976 open problem. The 2001 reprint date is separated from the 1971 circulation and publication.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The off-shell Wess--Zumino chiral multiplet
notes: The list is \(A\) scalar, \(B\) pseudoscalar, \(\psi\) again labelled scalar, and auxiliary \(F\) scalar, \(G\) pseudoscalar. A bracket groups the five fields as a supermultiplet.
statement: The four-dimensional \(N=1\) chiral multiplet comprises two real bosonic fields \(A,B\), one four-real-component Majorana fermion \(\psi\), and two real auxiliary bosons \(F,G\). Off shell it has four real bosonic and four real fermionic component functions; the auxiliary fields have no kinetic terms. The scalar label on \(\psi\) is incompatible with its gamma-matrix kinetic term and supersymmetry variations.
reconstruction: The spinor correction is compelled both by the following notebook formulas and the named model. The off-shell component count does not count propagating degrees of freedom.
fate: \citet[\S 3, chiral superfield; \S 4(b)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields} describes the pre-existing Wess--Zumino model, introduced in 1974.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established multiplet; \(\psi\) must be a spinor. No experimental discovery of a supersymmetric multiplet is implied.

title: A consistent supersymmetric action and the notebook’s coefficient defects
notes: Two formulas are named the Wess--Zumino Lagrangian, one after and one before eliminating \(F,G\). The latter has \(\bar\Psi\gamma^\beta\partial_\mu\Psi\) and a fermion mass coefficient differing by a factor 2 from the former.
statement: One consistent modern convention uses metric \((+---)\), a complex scalar \(\phi\), Weyl fermion \(\chi\), complex auxiliary field \(\mathcal F\), and holomorphic \(W(\phi)=m\phi^2/2+g\phi^3/3\): \[\mathcal L=\partial_\mu\bar\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi+i\bar\chi\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\chi+\bar{\mathcal F}\mathcal F+\bigl(\mathcal F W'(\phi)-\tfrac12W''(\phi)\chi\chi+\text{h.c.}\bigr).\] Here spinor contractions use the standard antisymmetric two-spinor pairing. This action has the intended chiral supersymmetry; it is not a term-for-term endorsement of the notebook's inconsistent real-component display.
reconstruction: The complex normalization, opposite metric convention and \(W\) are expressly modern reconstruction. In the notebook, the kinetic indices must contract; moreover eliminating bosonic auxiliary fields cannot change an untouched fermion mass coefficient from \(-im\) to \(-im/2\).
fate: The intended component construction is verified in \citet[\S 4(b), equations~4.12--4.23]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}, already in the December 1975 review.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The standard model is established. The literal pair of notebook Lagrangians is inconsistent and should not be used as a checked supersymmetric action.

title: Eliminating the auxiliary fields and auditing the potential
notes: Because no derivatives of \(F,G\) occur, their Euler equations are said to recover the preceding action. Its cubic scalar term is positive and its quartic coefficient is written ambiguously as \(g_2^2\).
statement: Using exactly the real auxiliary terms printed on P000669, \[\mathcal L_{\rm aux}=\tfrac12(F^2+G^2)+m(FA+GB)+g\{F(A^2-B^2)+2GAB\},\] their equations uniquely give \(F=-mA-g(A^2-B^2)\), \(G=-mB-2gAB\). Substitution yields \[-\tfrac12m^2(A^2+B^2)-mgA(A^2+B^2)-\tfrac12g^2(A^2+B^2)^2.\] Thus the cubic sign in P000668 is inconsistent with P000669; \(g^2/2\) is the forced quartic coefficient in these conventions.
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ Completing both squares independently verifies the substitution. The scan has no clear fraction bar at \(g_2^2\), so the quartic change is an evidence-based emendation, not a confident new paleographic reading.
fate: Auxiliary elimination is part of the pre-existing construction \citep[\S 4(b), equations~4.16 and 4.23]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}. The comparison here checks the notebook internally.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The algebraic elimination is exact. It diagnoses a faithful cubic-sign error and an ambiguous quartic notation; it does not repair all fermionic conventions automatically.

title: Infinitesimal supersymmetry and invariance of the action
notes: Five variations of \(A,B,\Psi,F,G\) are displayed, with \(\delta A=i\bar\alpha\Psi\), derivative terms in \(\delta\Psi\), and derivatives of \(\Psi\) in \(\delta F,\delta G\). The text says that the Lagrangian is invariant.
statement: In the consistent complex convention of the previous occurrence, take a constant Grassmann-odd Weyl parameter \(\epsilon\). The transformations \(\delta\phi=\sqrt2\epsilon\chi\), \(\delta\chi=i\sqrt2\sigma^\mu\bar\epsilon\,\partial_\mu\phi+\sqrt2\epsilon\mathcal F\), \(\delta\mathcal F=i\sqrt2\bar\epsilon\bar\sigma^\mu\partial_\mu\chi\), and their conjugates close off shell on translations. The variation of \(\mathcal L\) is a total derivative, so the action is invariant when boundary terms vanish. It is not necessary for the density to be pointwise unchanged.
reconstruction: Odd parameters, the use of an even variation operator and the total-derivative qualification are supplied. A term-by-term sign identification with the notebook's barred-Majorana conventions is not asserted.
fate: \citet[\S 1, equation~1.1; \S 4(b)]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields} verifies this pre-talk off-shell symmetry and component interpretation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established classical supersymmetry. The named action and multiplet are identified exactly, while the notebook's unexplained sign conventions receive only a partial formula match.

title: Valence quarks in nucleons and mesons
notes: A proton is drawn with three dots labelled ``3 quarks''; the last sentence says mesons are made from a quark and an antiquark.
statement: In the minimal valence-quark model, a proton has flavour content \(uud\), a neutron \(udd\), and ordinary mesons have \(q\bar q\) content. Colour singlets occur through \(\Lambda^3\mathbb C^3\cong\mathbb C\) for three quarks and the contraction \(\mathbb C^3\otimes(\mathbb C^3)^*\to\mathbb C\) for a quark--antiquark pair. These are valence classifications, not assertions that interacting hadrons contain exactly this number of quantum excitations.
reconstruction: The representation-theoretic singlet maps make the claim precise; gluons, sea pairs and nonminimal hadrons are not excluded.
fate: The pre-talk constituent picture is recalled by \citet[\S I]{wilson1974confinement}; the modern qualification is explicit in \citet[\S 15.1]{amslercredegrand2024quark}. It continues 1975-377.1.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The valence terminology remains standard with the stated limits; it is not an exact Fock-space decomposition theorem.
area: Quantum field theory and quark structure

title: Short-distance freedom seen through electromagnetic probes
notes: Quarks are said to be ``free inside'' and visible when the proton is probed by gamma quanta.
statement: The controlled theoretical statement is asymptotic freedom: for four-dimensional \(SU(3)\) gauge theory with \(N_f\) Dirac fermions in the fundamental representation and no additional scalar matter, \[\mu\frac{dg}{d\mu}=-\frac{11-2N_f/3}{16\pi^2}g^3+O(g^5).\] For \(N_f\le16\), the weak-coupling ultraviolet flow is toward \(g=0\). Deep-inelastic electromagnetic scattering probes short-distance charged constituents, with calculable scaling violations; it does not show exactly free quarks at all distances inside a hadron.
reconstruction: The beta-function formula and regime are supplied as the precise interpretation of the physical shorthand, not as a computation performed at this talk.
fate: \citet[equations~8--9]{grosswilczek1973ultraviolet} published the result 25 June 1973, received 27 April 1973, before the lecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established perturbative ultraviolet behaviour. It does not by itself prove long-distance confinement.

title: Confinement as a pre-existing physical programme
notes: The juxtaposed assertion is that quarks cannot be taken out of a nucleon and that the binding is associated with colour.
statement: The intended physical hypothesis is absence of isolated colour-charged asymptotic particles, while observable hadron states are colour singlets. A precise theorem would additionally require a defined quantum gauge theory, its physical Hilbert space and a specified confinement criterion. Those data are not supplied by this page. Cutoff-lattice strong-coupling confinement and continuum QCD confinement are different statements.
reconstruction: This records the prior physical programme without replacing the notes by a new request to solve the continuum Yang--Mills mass-gap problem.
fate: \citet[abstract and \S\S I--II]{wilson1974confinement} had already formulated a gauge-theoretic confinement mechanism and its lattice-cutoff limitation. \citet[\S 15.1]{amslercredegrand2024quark} still phrases general QCD confinement as a belief.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Class E marks pre-talk exposition, not a completed rigorous continuum proof. The notebook provides no unique additional unresolved mathematical scope to index as a new C/D problem.

title: A growing potential is not necessarily a growing force
notes: The emphatic sentence is:\par \ru{В теории силы должны расти с расстояниями!}
statement: In a static-source model, a confining potential \(V(R)\sim\sigma R\), \(\sigma>0\), has force magnitude \(|V'(R)|\sim\sigma\), not a force diverging with separation. Formally an area law \(\langle W(R,T)\rangle\sim e^{-\sigma RT}\) yields this linear potential via \(V(R)=-\lim_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\log\langle W(R,T)\rangle\), if that limit exists. With dynamical light quarks the asymptotic static-source problem also involves string breaking.
reconstruction: \ours\ Differentiating a linear potential suffices to refute the necessity of increasing force. The Wilson-loop limit is an explanatory reconstruction with its existence assumption explicit.
fate: The area-law mechanism is already in \citet[\S II and \S IV]{wilson1974confinement}; modern model and string-breaking qualifications appear in \citet[\S\S 15.7--15.8]{amslercredegrand2024quark}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The literal force requirement is false. The appropriate statement concerns energy cost and the specified static-source regime.

title: The uncertainty-principle slogan does not specify a stability theorem
notes: A short sentence says that by the uncertainty principle the quarks cannot merge.
statement: An uncertainty relation such as \(\Delta x\,\Delta p\ge\hbar/2\) gives a kinetic localization cost only after a state and Hamiltonian are specified. Whether that cost prevents collapse depends on the attractive interaction, particle statistics and relativistic regime. None of these quantitative data occurs in the sentence.
reconstruction: No particular many-body stability inequality or confining Hamiltonian is inferred.
fate: The exact stability assertion could not be identified in the searched confinement and quark-model sources; \citet[\S 15.7]{amslercredegrand2024quark} discusses models but cannot supply the missing Hamiltonian.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Unidentified as a mathematical result. The sentence is physical intuition, not an independent proof of confinement or noncollapse.

title: Local Lorentz-covariant gauge dynamics instead of a prescribed force law
notes: Relativistic invariance is said to obstruct a direct potential law; pointlike probing is offered as evidence for locality, and the proposed response is to construct Lagrangians and gauge fields.
statement:
A local classical model on Minkowski space uses an \(SU(3)\) connection \(A_\mu\), its curvature \(F_{\mu
u}\), and Dirac fields \(q_f\) in the colour fundamental representation, with \(\mathcal L=-	frac14F^a_{\mu
u}F^{a\mu
u}+\sum_f ar q_f(i\gamma^\mu D_\mu-m_f)q_f\). This is local, Lorentz covariant and invariant under smooth local colour changes. Small observed constituent size is evidence for a useful local-field model; it is not a proof of the exact quantum microcausality axiom.
reconstruction: The explicit Lagrangian is a labelled modern reconstruction of the proposed method; no action formula appears in Migdal's short notes.
fate: The covariant-derivative and curvature construction predates QCD: \citet[equations~2--11]{yangmills1954conservation}. Its colour application is already proposed in \citet[p.1345]{grosswilczek1973ultraviolet}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established classical gauge-theory framework. Defining its full nonperturbative continuum quantum dynamics is a separate task not formulated here.

title: Colour and flavour are two different indices
notes: The \(3\times3\) array has columns \(p,n,\lambda\) and rows 1,2,3. The vertical group is \(SU(3)\) colour, the horizontal flavour group is annotated ``unknown'', and the text says there are nine quarks.
statement: For the three light flavours, write \(q^a_f\), \(a=1,2,3\), \(f=u,d,s\). This gives nine colour--flavour components before spinor indices; it does not give nine flavours. A local colour matrix acts on \(a\), while a global flavour matrix acts on \(f\). With equal light-quark masses and electromagnetism omitted, vector \(SU(3)\) flavour is a symmetry; unequal masses break it. The full modern quark inventory has six flavours, each with three colours.
reconstruction: The traditional \(p,n,\lambda\) labels are interpreted as the light-flavour triplet, not physical proton/neutron/Lambda fields in the same gauge multiplet. The ``unknown'' annotation does not specify a unique unresolved group-classification problem.
fate: \citet[p.1345]{grosswilczek1973ultraviolet} already separates colour from global flavour symmetries. \citet[\S\S 15.1--15.2,15.5.1]{amslercredegrand2024quark} gives modern terminology. The seminar had already discussed four flavours and three colours in 1975-367.5.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: The nine-component light-flavour model is identifiable. Treating it as a complete inventory in 1976 would contradict the earlier seminar's four-flavour discussion; the shorthand is therefore not silently expanded into such a claim.
area: Quantum field theory and quark structure

title: Local colour gauge symmetry
notes: The last conceptual distinction says that the colour group corresponds to a much stronger symmetry, namely gauge symmetry.
statement: The gauge group consists locally of smooth maps \(U:M\to SU(3)\), acting by \(q_f\mapsto Uq_f\) and, for \(D=d+A\), \(A\mapsto UAU^{-1}-(dU)U^{-1}\). Then \(F\mapsto UFU^{-1}\). Constant colour rotations form a subgroup of this local transformation group. ``Stronger'' means freedom to choose the colour frame independently at each spacetime point, with the connection compensating derivatives.
reconstruction: This specifies the mathematical content of the comparison; gauge transformations describe redundancy of field variables and are not simply an extra independent global flavour action.
fate: \citet[isotopic gauge transformation, equations~1--5]{yangmills1954conservation} gives the local construction in 1954; the colour specialization predates the talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026: Established local gauge symmetry. No new gauge-group extension problem is posed by the sentence.
